E1.title: Report of Apollo 13 Review Board (NASA), NSSDC plain-text edition

C-a13-mission.text: Apollo 13 was launched from Kennedy Space Center
C-a13-mission.passage: Apollo 13 was successfully launched on schedule from Launch Complex 39A, Kennedy Space Center, Florida, at 2:13 p.m. e.s.t., April 11, 1970.

C-a13-launch.passage: Apollo 13 was successfully launched on schedule from Launch Complex 39A, Kennedy Space Center, Florida, at 2:13 p.m. e.s.t., April 11, 1970.

C-a13-detank-date.text: Detanking operations were resumed on March 27, 1970
C-a13-detank-date.passage: On Friday, March 27, 1970, detanking operations were resumed

C-a13-heaters-65v.text: During detanking the tank heaters were powered from the 65 V dc ground supply
C-a13-heaters-65v.passage: The heaters were energized with the 65 V dc. GSE power supply

C-a13-switch-rating.text: The thermostatic switches were rated for the 28 V dc spacecraft supply and could not open properly at 65 V dc
C-a13-switch-rating.passage: Subsequent investigations have shown that the thermostatic switches used, while rated as satisfactory for the 28 V dc spacecraft power supply, could not open properly at 65 V dc.

C-a13-switch-80f.text: Each thermostatic switch was intended to open the heater circuit at 80 F
C-a13-switch-80f.passage: each heater is protected with a thermostatic switch, mounted on the heater tube, which is intended to open the heater circuit when it senses a temperature of 80 F.

C-a13-1000f.text: Switch failure probably let the heater tube reach about 1000 F in spots during 8 hours of heater operation
C-a13-1000f.passage: failure of the thermostatic switches probably permitted the temperature of the heater tube assembly to reach about 1000 F in spots during the continuous 8-hour period of heater operation.

C-a13-teflon.text: That heating severely damages the Teflon insulation on the fan motor wires
C-a13-teflon.passage: Such heating has been shown by tests to severely damage the Teflon insulation on the fan motor wires in the vicinity of the heater assembly.

C-a13-hazard.text: From then on, including on the pad, oxygen tank no. 2 was hazardous when filled and powered
C-a13-hazard.passage: From that time on, including pad occupancy, the oxygen tank no. 2 was in a hazardous condition when filled with oxygen and electrically powered.

C-a13-fans.text: Current was applied to the oxygen tank no. 2 fan motors at 55:53:20 g.e.t.
C-a13-fans.passage: current was applied to the oxygen tank no. 2 fan motors at 55:53:20.

C-a13-dataloss.text: At 55:54:53.555 g.e.t. telemetry was lost almost totally for 1.8 seconds
C-a13-dataloss.passage: About 1-1/2 minutes later, at 55:54:53.555, telemetry from the spacecraft was lost almost totally for 1.8 seconds.

C-a13-pressure.text: Oxygen tank no. 2 lost pressure in that period and the panel separated
C-a13-pressure.passage: All indications are that the cryogenic oxygen tank no. 2 lost pressure in this time period and the panel separated.

C-a13-cause.text: An electrically initiated fire in oxygen tank no. 2 was the cause of the accident
C-a13-cause.passage: All indications are that an electrically initiated fire in oxygen tank no. 2 in the service module (SM) was the cause of the accident.
C-a13-cause.display: an electrically initiated fire|in oxygen tank no. 2

C-a13-averted.text: A near disaster averted only by the crew and the ground control team
C-a13-averted.passage: The imperfection in Apollo 13 constituted a near disaster, averted only by outstanding performance on the part of the crew and the ground control team which supported them.

C-a13-payoff.text: Editorial summary: the danger began on the ground; the mission was saved in space
C-a13-payoff.note: editorial summary of the board's findings; not a quotation
